newsitem.title: IRAQ: Saddam says Iranians may visit Iraq's holy shrines.
newsitem.headline: Saddam says Iranians may visit Iraq's holy shrines.

text.p: President Saddam Hussein has allowed visits by Iranians to Iraq's Shi'ite Molsem shrines, suspended since the beginning of the 1980-1988 Iraq-Iran war, to resume next month, Baghdad radio said on Monday.
"President Saddam Hussein has instructed the authorities concerned to allow Iranian citizens to visit holy shrines in Iraq as from September 4, 1997," the radio said, quoting an official spokesman.
There was no immediate reaction from Iran.
Shi'ites, who form the overwhelming majority of Iran's 60 million population, regard the shrines in Karbala and Najaf in southern Iraq as second only to Islam's holiest sites in Mecca and Medina.
Iranian visits to the shrines were suspended at the start of the Iraq-Iran war in which nearly one million people from the two sides were killed.
September 4 is the date Iraq says the war started in 1980. Iran says it began on September 22.

The radio said the decision on allowing Iranian pilgrims to visit Iraq was taken after a joint meeting of the Revolutionary Command Council, Iraq's highest authority, and the regional command of the ruling Baath party.
The spokesman urged the Iranian visitors to stick to Iraqi regulations and guidelines governing their visits and said.
"All should be alert to prevent those who have special intentions from destroying such an initiative which represents a window of contact and goodwill for the peoples of the two countries," he said.
The spokesman said the decision was taken despite problems still troubling Iraq's relations with its eastern neighbour which Saddam referred to in a speech this month.

In his August 8 speech Saddam urged new Iranian President Mohammad Khatami to free Iraqi prisoners of war and return to Iraq aircraft sent to Iran to escape bombings during the 1991 Gulf War over Kuwait.
Saddam said Iraq had freed all 39,000 Iranian POWs except for one pilot whose plane was shot down over Iraqi territory on September 18, 1980.
Khatami, who took office on August 4, urged Iraq on Sunday to free Iranian prisoners of war.
Iraq says more than 20,000 Iraqis are still held in Iran. Tehran denies this and says Baghdad is still holding 5,000 to 10,000 Iranian prisoners.
